currentContext.expansion: Max Estates' expansion is land- and project-led rather than plant-led, concentrated in Delhi-NCR (Noida and Gurugram) across commercial, residential and mixed-use asset classes, executed through dedicated project SPVs. On the commercial side, two large assets are under design and development: Max District, Sector 65 on Golf Course Extension Road, Gurugram - a ~4-acre parcel with ~0.9 mn sq. ft. of office area and 0.1 mn sq. ft. of retail within a 1.6 million sq. ft. leasable-area development, LEED Platinum and WiredScore Platinum pre-certified, progressing on track for occupancy certificates in two phases (Phase 1 in Q2 FY28 and Phase 2 in Q3 FY29), with 200,000 sq. ft. already pre-leased at a 35%+ premium to the micro-market locking in over Rs 270 crore of gross rentals over a nine-year term two-and-a-half years before completion; and Max Square Two, Sector 129 Noida - a 7.35-acre parcel with ~1.6 mn sq. ft. leasable area (project stated at 1 million sq. ft. leasable), IGBC Platinum pre-certified with WELL certification under process, on track for its occupation certificate by Q2 FY28, with ~86,000 sq. ft. pre-leased at a ~25% premium securing over Rs 95 crore of gross rentals. Together with the delivered assets (Max House Phases I and II, Max Towers, Max Square, all at 100% occupancy), the commercial portfolio - delivered, under-construction and acquisition-stage - is positioned to reach annuity rental income potential exceeding Rs 700 crore on a 100% basis over the next five years. On the residential side the pipeline GDV exceeds Rs 17,200 crore: Estate 361 (18 acres, ~4 mn sq. ft. saleable, Rs 9,000 crore overall potential) launched Phase 1 in Q3 FY26 at ~Rs 2,500 crore GDV and added The Terraces precinct in May 2026 with an incremental Rs 1,200 crore of GDV; Estate 105, Sector 105 Noida (~10 acres, ~2.6 mn sq. ft. potential) was launched in March 2026 at ~Rs 3,000 crore initial GDV and repositioned to a residential plus serviced-apartment mix that doubled GDV potential to ~Rs 6,000 crore, with Phase 2 planned for FY27; and Sector 59, Golf Course Extension Road Gurugram (7.25 acres, ~1.3 mn sq. ft. potential, GDV potential Rs 3,900+ crore) is targeted for launch in Q4 FY27. Inorganic footprint additions during FY26 were made through SPV acquisitions - Boulevard Projects Private Limited (acquired 23 April 2025, enabling the revival of the stalled "Delhi One" development in Sector 16B Noida as Max One after RERA clearances) and Base Buildwell Private Limited (acquired 26 December 2025, the Sector 59 Gurugram land parcel, total transaction outlay ~Rs 534.32 crore covering share capital, security deposit, purchase of Transferable Development Rights and related approvals) - alongside incorporation of two new wholly-owned subsidiaries, Max Estates Noida Two Limited (1 September 2025) and Max Estates Developers Limited (30 January 2026). Capacity to execute is being built out on the organisational side too: the workforce expanded to 309 permanent employees with 129 onboarded across 20 functions in FY26 (about 10x headcount growth over the last few years), SOPs institutionalised across 13 critical verticals of the value chain, and a digital ecosystem (SAP, Salesforce, Ozonetel, Reloy and HR platforms) deployed to support scale. Funding for the Noida build-out was secured through a Rs 584 crore Compulsory Convertible Debenture co-investment with New York Life Insurance Company (NYL Rs 293 crore, Max Estates Rs 291 crore), with FY26 concluded at negligible net debt and residential execution funded through internal accruals.

risks.risk: Single-activity concentration - 100% of turnover from real estate
risks.note: BRSR Section A reports Real Estate (including facility management, with owned or leased assets) as the sole business activity at 100% of turnover, and Real Estate Development as the sole product/service at 100% of turnover. There is no second earnings stream to cushion a downturn in the property cycle.

The Company states it "has strategically chosen to focus currently on developing multiple asset classes in Delhi NCR", with exports not applicable and registered/corporate offices only in Noida (UP), Okhla (New Delhi) and Gurugram (Haryana). Regulatory, approval, infrastructure or demand shocks specific to the NCR micro-markets hit the entire portfolio at once.

Flagged as a Risk in the BRSR material responsible business conduct issues table: "Non-compliance with environmental regulations can result in penalties, legal consequences, and reputational harm", with negative financial implications of potential fines, legal costs and reputational damage. Mitigation is an environmental management system, adherence to regulations, monitoring and reporting, and a zero-tolerance policy on non-compliance.

Flagged as a Risk in the BRSR material issues table, citing increasing climate-related events (floods, heatwaves, thunderstorms, smog situations) - relevant for a business whose construction schedules, site safety and operating assets are exposed to weather and air-quality disruption.

risks.risk: Execution and approval dependency on new land/SPV acquisitions
risks.note: The Board's Report qualifies the projected booking value of more than Rs 3,000 crore from the Base Buildwell (Sector 59, Gurugram) acquisition as "subject to project execution timelines, requisite approvals and market conditions", making a material part of the growth pipeline contingent on regulatory clearance and market absorption.

BRSR transparency disclosures record 1,662 customer complaints filed in FY 2025-26 against 914 in FY 2024-25 (classified as Commercial and Residential, none related to delivery of essential services), all closed with none pending. The near-doubling alongside portfolio scale-up is a service-quality and brand watch-item; Factech Software has been implemented across all commercial operational sites.

Permanent employee turnover was 16% in FY 2025-26 (14% male, 25% female) versus 15% in FY 2024-25 and 18% in FY 2023-24. With women at only 17% of the workforce, the materially higher female attrition rate works against the stated diversity agenda and against retention of a workforce being scaled to support the project pipeline.

risks.risk: Legacy shareholder/legal matter at a subsidiary
risks.note: A BRSR grievance note records a complaint pertaining to "a legacy matter involving a former shareholder of Pharmax Corporation Limited, a Subsidiary of the Company" - a residual claim carried in through an acquired SPV, illustrating inherited-liability exposure in the acquisition-led growth model.

risks.risk: Partial ownership of material operating subsidiaries
risks.note: Several material project SPVs are not wholly owned - Max Towers Private Limited, Max Square Limited, Pharmax Corporation Limited and Acreage Builders Private Limited are each 51%-held and Max Estates Noida Private Limited is 60%-held - so a meaningful share of asset-level economics accrues to non-controlling interests and requires partner alignment.

risks.risk: No external assurance on the BRSR/sustainability disclosures
risks.note: BRSR Section A items 14 and 15 record the name of assurance provider and type of assurance obtained as "Not Applicable", so the ESG data underpinning the sustainability narrative is unassured.

one-line thesis: Max Estates delivered a record Q4 with INR 3,300 cr bookings driven by successful launches (Estate 105, Max One), crossing INR 5,300 cr full-year presales for the second consecutive year. The company sits on a massive locked-in revenue pipeline (INR 12,500 cr sold but unrecognized) and a near-net-zero debt position, positioning it to scale annuity income to INR 700 cr over 5 years despite near-term geopolitical caution.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 200 cr (FY26); EBITDA: INR 24 cr (12% margin); PAT: INR 23 cr (low base due to revenue recognition timing vs. booking surge); Order Book: INR 16,310 cr total pipeline (INR 12,500 cr sold/locked); Net Debt: ~INR 100 cr (Gross Debt INR 1,850 cr less Cash INR 1,750 cr). One-offs: Significant Ind AS rental equalization adjustment boosted Q4 commercial revenue; Max One acquisition involved recognizing INR 1,200 cr inherited sales as new bookings post-RERA.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Implicit strong growth from INR 12.5k cr locked pipeline; Margin: Targeting established bands despite inflation (contingencies built in); Order Inflow: No explicit FY27 presales guidance due to macro caution, but INR 17k cr GDV pipeline ready; Capex/Commissioning: Max Square Two (Q2 FY28), Max District (Q2 FY28 & Q3 FY29).
order book & pipeline: Total launch project revenue pending recognition: INR 16,310 cr; Sold & Contracted (locked): INR 12,500 cr; Embedded PBT: INR 4,200-4,900 cr; Residential Pipeline GDV: >INR 17,200 cr.
segment / subsidiary detail: Residential: FY26 Presales INR 5,305 cr (+70% CAGR since FY24); Q4 Bookings INR 3,300 cr; Collections INR 1,578 cr (+61% YoY); Avg Realization INR 23,000/sqft. Commercial: 100% occupancy across 3 assets (1.2 mn sqft); Rental Income INR 150 cr (+40% YoY); Pre-leasing secured INR 365 cr+ gross rentals (Max District & Max Square Two).
growth verticals / optionality: Launching 'The Terraces' (INR 1,200 cr GDV) and Sector 59 Gurgaon (INR 3,900 cr GDV) in FY27; Repositioning Estate 105 doubled GDV to INR 6,000 cr; Targeting annual addition of 2 mn sqft residential and 1 mn sqft commercial; Exploring TOD projects in Delhi.
margins & cost dynamics: Inflationary pressures acknowledged (West Asia conflict); Mitigated via built-in escalation clauses and contingency budgets in project costing; Management confident in achieving guided margin bands.
capex / expansion: Funded primarily via internal accruals and RERA surplus (INR 1,200 cr); Construction finance tied for commercial assets to be refinanced via Lease Rental Discounting (LRD) upon leasing stabilization; No land acquisition debt strategy.
capital allocation: Prioritizing organic growth and value-accretive acquisitions (e.g., Max One); Maintaining lean balance sheet (Net Debt ~INR 100 cr); Surplus cash deployed into construction; Dividend policy not explicitly detailed but implied capacity given cash position.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical tension (West Asia) impacting sentiment and input costs; Regulatory changes (Delhi TOD rules, land pooling); Execution risk on large pipeline deliveries; Market moderation in NCR luxury segment.
management quality / tone: Cautiously Optimistic; Disciplined; Confident in brand power and end-user demand despite macro headwinds; Transparent on accounting nuances.
non-obvious takeaways: INR 12,500 cr of revenue is already sold and contracted but not yet recognized, creating a high-visibility earnings runway; The 'Max One' acquisition allowed recognition of INR 1,200 cr inherited sales as fresh bookings, artificially inflating current presales metrics while providing future annuity upside from unsold portion.

themes.title: Real-estate up-cycle - premium housing & redevelopment
themes.need: The residential up-cycle is now presales-led with a visible margin cost. SOBHA posted its highest-ever presales at INR 3,656cr (+76% YoY, 2.34 msf at an average INR 15,655/sqft, NCR at a record INR 1,384cr) and guided FY27 presales at +30% or better - but reported EBITDA is still only ~9.7%, guided to 17-20% only by exit-Q4, and forthcoming-project marginal cash flow was cut from ~INR 86bn to INR 68.3bn on a heavier joint-development mix. SUNTECK booked INR 787cr of presales (+20%) with ZERO launches in the quarter, with aspirational-luxury (Naigaon/Kalyan) at 21% of presales 'picking up because of the lower interest rate' - the first sign the rate-elastic end is turning on demand rather than inventory release. DLF's FY26 bookings of INR20,143cr and 50mn sq ft of rental at 95% occupancy anchor the annuity leg; LODHA/GODREJPROP/PRESTIGE-tier and MMR redevelopers (RUSTOMJEE, KALPATARU, RAYMONDREL, MANINFRA, SURAJEST) ride premiumization; PHOENIXLTD/EMBDL on mixed-use.
themes.driver: SOBHA's exit-Q4 margin ramp from ~9.7% to 17-20% is the falsifiable claim (JD-heavy growth structurally lowers marginal margins); rate-elastic aspirational absorption (SUNTECK); FY27 launch-pipeline execution and festive booking momentum.

themes.title: Flexible workspace, PropTech & commercial real-estate services
themes.need: The GCC build-out and hybrid-work shift drive managed/flexible office demand, and Q1FY27 showed flex becoming the marginal buyer of Indian office space. SMARTWORKS grew revenue 44% to INR 546cr with normalized EBITDA INR 107cr (+74%) at a 19.6% margin, lifted GCC clients from 15% to 21% of revenue in a single quarter, and reported India's highest-ever quarterly leasing at 24.6 mn sq ft with 27% of it through flex, up from 19% a year ago. PropTech consolidation started in the same quarter: AURUM announced the acquisition of Housing.com (~24% of India's online-portal share, 58mn monthly visits) at ~1.5x revenue against listed comparables at 4.5-10x, with Housing currently burning ~INR 200cr a year and committed to break even in four to six quarters. AWFIS/EFCIL/INDIQUBE/DEVX/WEWORK add managed workspace; NIRLON on office REIT-proxy assets.
themes.driver: GCC seat-count additions and flex share of net leasing; AURUM's four-to-six-quarter Housing.com breakeven clock; enterprise managed-office wins.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Max Estates Limited is the real estate development arm of the Max Group, positioned as a "real estate well-being enabler" that develops commercial, residential and mixed-use spaces in Delhi NCR around its LiveWell, WorkWell and PlayWell principles.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Max Estates develops and operates Grade A+ commercial office campuses, premium/luxury residential communities and mixed-use developments, currently focused on Delhi NCR (Noida, Gurugram, New Delhi) with one residential community in Dehradun. Projects are executed through dedicated project SPVs and are designed around well-being, sustainability, biophilia and community amenities, with green/wellness certifications (LEED, IGBC, WELL, WiredScore) pursued across the portfolio. It serves two customer sets: commercial occupiers (WorkWell) spanning professional services, financial services, IT/ITES, media, real-estate-related businesses and manufacturing, and premium/luxury homebuyers (LiveWell), with senior-living offerings managed by Antara Senior Living Limited.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's domestic economy remained stable and resilient with FY26 real GDP growth estimated at 7.4%, the fastest-growing major economy for the fourth consecutive year, supported by steady consumption, historically low inflation and robust investment - against a fragile global environment of geopolitical tensions and trade fragmentation
- India's real estate market continued to consolidate: rising household incomes, infrastructure development and premiumisation supported demand even as participation by smaller developers in new launches declined
- New supply is becoming increasingly concentrated among branded, diversified developers with prudent balance sheets; relatively low inventory overhang gives them headroom to sustain launches, accelerate asset churn and capture market share
- Residential sales entered a more calibrated phase, but demand for premium and luxury housing remained resilient across major cities, supported by shifting lifestyle preferences and strong end-user demand
- Delhi-NCR continued to stand out as one of India's most dynamic real estate markets with strong traction across premium residential and commercial assets, reinforcing the relevance of the focused NCR strategy
- Residential collections follow a disciplined payment structure delivering steady annual collections of around 20-25% of total sales value, giving predictable cash flow to fund construction from internal accruals
- Commercial annuity income trajectory is maturing rapidly across delivered, under-construction and acquisition-stage assets, providing a long-dated institutional income stream
- Grade A workspace demand keeps operational commercial assets at 100% occupancy, and forward leasing is being locked in at a premium to prevailing micro-market rates
- Solar power implementation at Max Square cuts electricity costs by 20% to 25% alongside an annual emission reduction of 6,000 tonnes - an operating cost lever
- Scale-up of headcount (10x growth over the last few years; 129 professionals onboarded in FY26 with focused hiring in the residential vertical) to support upcoming high-value launches
- Cumulative residential presales to date of Rs 12,500 crore
- Future pipeline with a Gross Development Value exceeding Rs 17,200 crore
- FY26 record presales of Rs 5,305 crore - second consecutive year of surpassing the Rs 5,000 crore milestone; FY26 collections up 61% Y-o-Y to Rs 1,578 crore
- Estate 361: Rs 1,704 crore of presales with over 68% of Phase 1-launched inventory (GDV Rs 2,500 crore) cleared; The Terraces precinct introduced in May 2026 adds Rs 1,200 crore of GDV to a master project with overall potential of Rs 9,000 crore
- Estate 105: launched March 2026 with an initial GDV of ~Rs 3,000 crore and achieved ~Rs 1,783 crore of presales within ten days; repositioning has doubled GDV potential to ~Rs 6,000 crore ahead of a planned Phase 2 launch in FY27
- Max One (revival of the stalled "Delhi One" development, Sector 16B Noida): contributed ~Rs 1,415 crore to FY26 presales, including Rs 1,221 crore recognised post receipt of RERA that had been booked by the erstwhile developer
- Estate 360: cumulative presales booking value of Rs 4,831 crore alongside collections of Rs 1,636 crore, with construction progressing as planned
- Sector 59, Golf Course Extension Road, Gurugram: development rights secured with GDV potential of Rs 3,900+ crore, launch targeted for Q4 FY27
- Commercial operating assets (Max Towers, Max House Phases I & II, Max Square) at 100% occupancy generating aggregate annual rentals of Rs 158 crore
- Max District pre-leasing agreement locking in over Rs 270 crore of gross rentals over a nine-year term, secured two-and-a-half years before scheduled completion at a 35% premium to micro-market rates
- Max Square Two: ~86,000 sq. ft. pre-leased securing over Rs 95 crore in gross rentals, with a robust leasing pipeline maintained across both flagship assets
- Commercial portfolio annuity rental income potential exceeding Rs 700 crore on a 100% basis over the next five years

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Max Estates' expansion is land- and project-led rather than plant-led, concentrated in Delhi-NCR (Noida and Gurugram) across commercial, residential and mixed-use asset classes, executed through dedicated project SPVs. On the commercial side, two large assets are under design and development: Max District, Sector 65 on Golf Course Extension Road, Gurugram - a ~4-acre parcel with ~0.9 mn sq. ft. of office area and 0.1 mn sq. ft. of retail within a 1.6 million sq. ft. leasable-area development, LEED Platinum and WiredScore Platinum pre-certified, progressing on track for occupancy certificates in two phases (Phase 1 in Q2 FY28 and Phase 2 in Q3 FY29), with 200,000 sq. ft. already pre-leased at a 35%+ premium to the micro-market locking in over Rs 270 crore of gross rentals over a nine-year term two-and-a-half years before completion; and Max Square Two, Sector 129 Noida - a 7.35-acre parcel with ~1.6 mn sq. ft. leasable area (project stated at 1 million sq. ft. leasable), IGBC Platinum pre-certified with WELL certification under process, on track for its occupation certificate by Q2 FY28, with ~86,000 sq. ft. pre-leased at a ~25% premium securing over Rs 95 crore of gross rentals. Together with the delivered assets (Max House Phases I and II, Max Towers, Max Square, all at 100% occupancy), the commercial portfolio - delivered, under-construction and acquisition-stage - is positioned to reach annuity rental income potential exceeding Rs 700 crore on a 100% basis over the next five years. On the residential side the pipeline GDV exceeds Rs 17,200 crore: Estate 361 (18 acres, ~4 mn sq. ft. saleable, Rs 9,000 crore overall potential) launched Phase 1 in Q3 FY26 at ~Rs 2,500 crore GDV and added The Terraces precinct in May 2026 with an incremental Rs 1,200 crore of GDV; Estate 105, Sector 105 Noida (~10 acres, ~2.6 mn sq. ft. potential) was launched in March 2026 at ~Rs 3,000 crore initial GDV and repositioned to a residential plus serviced-apartment mix that doubled GDV potential to ~Rs 6,000 crore, with Phase 2 planned for FY27; and Sector 59, Golf Course Extension Road Gurugram (7.25 acres, ~1.3 mn sq. ft. potential, GDV potential Rs 3,900+ crore) is targeted for launch in Q4 FY27. Inorganic footprint additions during FY26 were made through SPV acquisitions - Boulevard Projects Private Limited (acquired 23 April 2025, enabling the revival of the stalled "Delhi One" development in Sector 16B Noida as Max One after RERA clearances) and Base Buildwell Private Limited (acquired 26 December 2025, the Sector 59 Gurugram land parcel, total transaction outlay ~Rs 534.32 crore covering share capital, security deposit, purchase of Transferable Development Rights and related approvals) - alongside incorporation of two new wholly-owned subsidiaries, Max Estates Noida Two Limited (1 September 2025) and Max Estates Developers Limited (30 January 2026). Capacity to execute is being built out on the organisational side too: the workforce expanded to 309 permanent employees with 129 onboarded across 20 functions in FY26 (about 10x headcount growth over the last few years), SOPs institutionalised across 13 critical verticals of the value chain, and a digital ecosystem (SAP, Salesforce, Ozonetel, Reloy and HR platforms) deployed to support scale. Funding for the Noida build-out was secured through a Rs 584 crore Compulsory Convertible Debenture co-investment with New York Life Insurance Company (NYL Rs 293 crore, Max Estates Rs 291 crore), with FY26 concluded at negligible net debt and residential execution funded through internal accruals.
